spec.name: int-sdiv-minus-one-runtime-args-p2

panel.evidence: divArgs(-32768, -1) reverted on EVM but succeeded on Polkadot. Solang stored last=-32768 and count=1, indicating it produced the wrapped int16 quotient INT16_MIN / -1 == INT16_MIN instead of reverting.
panel.rationale: Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic requires INT16_MIN / -1 to panic/revert because +32768 is outside the int16 range. The observed EVM revert matches that semantic rule, while solang both returns and persists the wrapped result. This is not an oracle projection or chain-environment artifact because the statuses and committed state differ.
panel.cluster_hint: missing checked-overflow revert for signed narrow integer division INT16_MIN / -1

panel.evidence: divArgs(-32768, -1) on int16: EVM reverts (arithmetic overflow panic, Solidity 0.8 checked math for INT16_MIN / -1), while Polkadot reports success and commits storage last=-32768, count=1. Solang performed the division without detecting the overflow, wrapping to -32768.
panel.rationale: Solidity 0.8 semantics require a runtime revert for signed division overflow (INT16_MIN / -1), and solc correctly reverts. Solang instead silently wraps and persists the bogus quotient plus an incremented counter, so this is a genuine missing-overflow-check semantic defect, not an environment or oracle artifact. The storage-count divergence merely reflects that solang committed state while EVM reverted, consistent with the status mismatch.
panel.cluster_hint: solang missing runtime overflow check for signed division of type minimum by -1 (wraps instead of reverting)

adversarial.evidence: EVM dry-run and committed transaction revert for divArgs(-32768, -1), matching Solidity 0.8 checked-arithmetic semantics (INT16_MIN / -1 overflows int16, panic 0x11). Polkadot reports success and commits storage last=-32768, count=1, i.e., solang wrapped the quotient to INT16_MIN and persisted state. Neither documented known-difference (env-values, gas-metering) applies: no environment markers, no gas comparison. No oracle projection is plausible because the oracle compares statuses and storage committed by each chain, and the divergence is directly explained by solang executing the division without the required overflow trap.
adversarial.rationale: The test is a minimal, valid probe of a single well-defined semantic rule: Solidity >=0.8 requires a runtime revert for signed division overflow of the type minimum by -1. Solang silently wraps and commits state, which is a genuine semantic defect, not a platform difference. The supplied historical record PR #1496 ('The negate operator - now checks for overflow at runtime, and other math overflow fixes') shows solang's developers explicitly treat missing narrow-integer overflow checks as bugs to fix, but it does not document signed division overflow as known/intentional behavior, so this is not a covered known difference or confirmed rediscovery. The evidence survives scrutiny.

history.title: v0.3.2 Brasília
history.text:
The language server is much improved, and many fixes all over.

### Added
- Go to definition is now implemented in the language server. [chioni16](https://github.com/chioni16)
- The parser has been updated to be compatible with Ethereum Solidity v0.8.21. [seanyoung](https://github.com/seanyoung)

### Fixed
- **breaking** Resolving import paths now matches solc more closely, and only resolves relative paths when specified as `./foo` or `../foo`. [seanyoung](https://github.com/seanyoung)
- **Solana** The `lamports` and `data` fields of `tx.accounts` can be modified again. [LucasSte](https://github.com/LucasSte)
- It is not longer necessary to save a Solidity file, in order for the language server to pick up changes to the file. [chioni16](https://github.com/chioni16)
- The negate operator `-` now checks for overflow at runtime, and other math overflow fixes. [seanyoung](https://github.com/seanyoung)

### Changed
- The Substrate target has been renamed to Polkadot. [xermicus](https://github.com/xermicus)
- **Polkadot** `assert()` and `require()` is now implemented as a transction revert, rather than a trap. The error data is returned, and encoded the same as on Ethereum.
